svg.text: SH-ESP32 proto area layout: two-NPN SeaTalk interface (R_b1 / R_pd1 swapped)
Top view, component side. Circuit: docs/seatalk-sh-esp32-npn.svg. Grid from the Rev 2.0 render; check pad labels on your Rev 2.1 board before soldering.
Coloured lines are bare-wire links / solder bridges on the BOTTOM side. Seen from the bottom, columns run T to B (mirror image).
GPIO header (top edge of board, right of the proto area)
Nets (bottom-side links; join every hole listed)
SeaTalk DATA (yellow): B4–G4, G3–G4, H3–G3, G4–G6, G6–H6
Parts (top side, leads through these holes)
R1 10 kΩ: C3, G3 R_b2 100 kΩ: H3, L3 R_pd2 22 kΩ (20 kΩ ok): M3, Q3
R_c 10 kΩ: H1, L1 R_b1 2.2 kΩ: I4, M4 R_pd1 10 kΩ: J5, N5
Q1 2N3904: C=H6 B=I6 E=J6 Q2 2N3904: C=L2 B=M2 E=N2 (flat face toward row 1 on both)
Wires: edge pads 3/4/5 to B3/B4/B5 (dashed, insulated). K2 to GPIO27. N4 to GPIO26.
Flat face toward row 1 means the round side faces the GND corner row. Seen from row 1 looking at the flat face: E-B-C left to right.
H4 and H5 are left empty on purpose: they separate DATA (G4-G6) from the Q1 base net (I4-I6).
Before power-up, with nothing connected, check: DATA to GND reads ~1 MΩ or more (not a few kΩ); 3.3 V to GND is not a short;
GPIO27 (K2) to 3.3 V reads 10 kΩ; DATA (B4) to +12 V (B3) reads ~10 kΩ. Then remove R_in and the old opto wiring from DATA.
